subject: Late-stage availability flag + mitigation & ops plan for Atlas Industries (RED-8934)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-02-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Late-stage availability flag for Atlas (RED-8934) — quick check

Team,

Atlas (RED-8934) just signaled a tighten on their timeline — they want a committed Dedicated pool available for a May onboarding. This is late-stage and procurement is asking for an internal availability confirmation by EOD tomorrow.

Ask: can infra/capacity confirm whether we can hold the equivalent of 8x A100-class slots (or 12x T4-equivalent staging) in our US east pool for their onboarding window (May 6–20)? If we can’t, list the minimum guaranteed set and the mitigation path (burst from spare pool, cross-region fallback, or temporary preemptible nodes).

What I need from each of you:
- Karthik: quick capacity snapshot + suggested MOQ for a soft hold
- Dev: any infra constraints (maintenance windows, node decommission plans) that would block a hold in May
- Neha: I'll need the list of Atlas contacts to coordinate contractual hold language (procurement cc’d)

Attached: previous roster snapshot (gpu_roster_v2.xlsx) — please update delta rows inline in your reply.

Thanks — short on time here.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-02-14T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Late-stage availability flag for Atlas (RED-8934) — quick check

Jordan —

Quick snapshot from the east fleet as of this morning (pulled from roster):
- Physically idle A100-class equivalents: 6 slots (can be reserved)
- Near-idle (scheduled jobs but can be rescheduled with 48h notice): 9 slots
- T4/generic staging units available: ~22 slots across pools

Initial recommendation:
- Soft hold: reserve 6 A100-equivalent now (low risk) + earmark an additional 4 by tagging 4 near-idle nodes as "probable-for-RED-8934" — this gives us 10 A100-equivalent with a 48–72h operational lead if we need to solidify.
- Contingency: if Atlas requires strict hard commit for all 8 A100s, we should plan for cross-region fallback to a west pool (adds ~25–40ms latency) or offer 12xT4 equivalent for staging/initial ramp.

Constraints / caveats:
- Node firmware update window scheduled 2029-04-28–04-30 — we should avoid hard commitments that overlap that window unless we can shift maintenance earlier.
- Capacity in east already has two other Q2 soft-holds (see comments in gpu_roster_v2.xlsx) — I updated the sheet with my delta rows (attachment).

Attachment: gpu_roster_v2.xlsx (updated)

I'll defer to Dev for infra-side blockers.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Capacity Planner | Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-02-14T13:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Late-stage availability flag for Atlas (RED-8934) — quick check

Jordan / team,

Confirming the maintenance window Karthik mentioned — we're planning a rolling firmware refresh across 40% of the east cluster end of April. That can be moved earlier by one week if needed, but shifting has downstream impacts on testing and some tenant schedules.

Operational notes and mitigations:
- Hard hold (contract-backed): we can carve out 6 A100-class nodes immediately; guaranteeing 8+ for the entire May window requires either:
  * a) Move the firmware window to Apr 21–23 (risk: compresses QA), or
  * b) Reserve 6 now and run a staged ramp using 12xT4 for weeks 1–2 of the onboarding, then swap-in A100s as they free up (works if Atlas accepts a two-stage approach).
- Burst option: we have a spare west pool that can provide up to 4 A100-equivalents with cross-region routing; ops will need Atlas to accept the latency delta and a fallback policy.

Action items I can do this week:
- Lock the 6-node soft carve and tag them in the roster (I will add do-not-schedule flag).
- Draft a short maintenance-shift impact note for the infra calendar if Jordan confirms they want a hard hold.

Attachment: none (I updated gpu_roster_v2.xlsx in Karthik's reply)

—Dev Patel
Infrastructure Lead, Dedicated Pools | Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Maya R. <maya@atlasind.com>
Cc: procurement@atlasind.com, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-02-14T15:07:00-08:00
Subject: Atlas onboarding window — proposed two-stage commitment and ask for confirmation

Maya —

Thanks for the call earlier. Internal check is underway. Short summary of our proposed path for your May onboarding:

1) Week 0–2 (initial onboarding): we provision a 12xT4-equivalent staging pool to match your early traffic pattern while we finalize A100 availability.
2) Week 3 onward: we swap-in A100-class nodes up to 8 committed units (target) as they are freed from near-idle scheduling.

We can soft-reserve 6 A100-equivalent nodes now and earmark an additional 4 with 48–72h lead time (per the attached internal roster). If you need a contract-backed hard commit for 8 A100s for the whole May window, we will need to shift a planned firmware maintenance earlier (operationally doable but will compress testing).

Please confirm which option you prefer: a) two-stage approach (staging + swap-in) or b) hard commit for 8 A100s (I will initiate the maintenance shift request). Procurement looped in.

Regards,
—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachment: mop_action_items.pdf (summary of proposed actions)

From: Maya R. <maya@atlasind.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, procurement@atlasind.com
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-02-15T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Atlas onboarding window — proposed two-stage commitment and ask for confirmation

Jordan / team —

Thanks for the quick turn. Procurement here prefers option (a) — the two-stage approach. Atlas is comfortable starting on T4s during initial ramp as long as the timeline to dedicated A100s is guaranteed and documented (we need an SLA addendum showing expected swap-in window and a rollback policy if swap-in is delayed).

Please send the short SLA addendum language and the internal operational contact who will authorize the swap. Procurement will review and push contract redlines next week.

—Maya R.
Senior Procurement Manager | Atlas Industries
